assumptions: Capture reagents and particle-count instruments have sufficient sensitivity and validated buffer compatibility for low-biomass lavage/CSF samples.
Short post-dose intervals increase chance of detecting nasally delivered intact EVs in proximal compartments if present.
Ex vivo cytokine readouts (e.g., IL-6/TNF-α) are an appropriate short-term functional proxy for neuroinflammation-modulating activity.
biological_rationale: Rodent intranasal efficacy signals exist but do not establish intact-EV exposure or mechanism. An orthogonal in vivo→ex vivo bridge that verifies intact-EV presence in short-interval nasal/CSF/olfactory-mucosa samples and links that verified exposure to an ex vivo cytokine modulation (abolished by membrane disruption) would provide mechanistic evidence that activity is EV-associated rather than driven by soluble secretome co-isolates.

candidate_quality_attributes.measurement_concept: Qualitative pass/fail: detection of capture-positive particle-co-localized fractions recoverable in lavage/CSF/tissue and associated ex vivo cytokine modulation abolished by membrane disruption.
candidate_quality_attributes.name: Intact-EV-associated, membrane-protected bioactivity (mechanism-linked potency)
candidate_quality_attributes.rationale: Links an orthogonal intact-EV identity signature to a short-interval ex vivo CNS inflammatory modulation after intranasal dosing; distinguishes EV-associated activity from bulk particle counts or soluble secretome activity.
candidate_quality_attributes.uncertainty: High: requires in vivo verification and careful negative controls; cross-species translation uncertain.

edges.competing_explanation: Observed ex vivo modulation could result from soluble secretome components that reach sampled compartments independently of intact EVs.
edges.missing_experiment: An orthogonal in vivo→ex vivo bridging experiment comparing capture-positive material versus membrane-disrupted and capture-depleted controls with short-interval tissue/fluid sampling.
edges.uncertainty: High: rodent efficacy supports potential functional effect but does not prove intact-EV exposure or cross-species translation.

edges.competing_explanation: Failure to detect in vivo exposure could arise from assay insensitivity, labeling artifacts, or administration/formulation differences rather than true absence of intact EVs.
edges.missing_experiment: A matched intact-EV verification assay in short-interval in vivo samples concurrent with ex vivo functional readout.
edges.uncertainty: Moderate: large-animal negative biodistribution raises concern that intact-EV exposure after intranasal dosing may be unreliable across species.

nodes.statement: An orthogonal intact-EV signature (capture-positive co-localization with particle peaks and detergent/protease-sensitive captured signal) identifies a membrane-protected EV fraction in source material.

If orthogonally verified intact-EV exposure is demonstrable in nasal lavage/CSF/olfactory-mucosa after intranasal dosing, then an ex vivo short-interval CNS inflammatory readout will be reproducibly modulated by captured material eluted from those compartments.

If the captured material is membrane-disrupted prior to administration or the administered material lacks the intact-EV signature, the ex vivo modulation will be abolished or qualitatively different, indicating activity is not intact-EV-associated.

competing_explanations: Soluble secretome components or co-isolated non-vesicular particles mediate observed functional effects.
Species-, formulation-, or delivery-related barriers, not intrinsic material identity, account for lack of in vivo detectability in larger animals.
dependencies: Analytical validation of capture sensitivity/specificity and buffer compatibility prior to in vivo sampling.
Availability of an exogenous intact-EV spike-in tracer for assay recovery controls (recommended).
Ethics and animal use approvals for short-interval sampling.
design_question: Can an orthogonally verified, intact-EV-associated, membrane-protected fraction (capture-positive and detergent/protease-sensitive co-localizing with particle peaks) predict a reproducible short-interval ex vivo CNS inflammatory modulation after intranasal dosing, independent of bulk particle counts?
expected_measurable_effect: Only material that is orthogonally verified as capture-positive, particle-co-localized, and detergent/protease-sensitive in source material and recoverable as capture-positive in short-interval lavage/CSF/tissue will produce a reproducible reduction in ex vivo inflammatory cytokine readouts; membrane-disrupted or capture-negative but particle-count-matched materials will not.

experiment.assay: Integrated protocol: (A) characterize administered materials in vitro with orthogonal intact-EV workflow (density fractionation + particle counts + immuno-capture + detergent/protease protection); (B) intranasal administration to rodents with short post-dose interval followed by collection of nasal lavage, CSF (if feasible), and olfactory-mucosa/olfactory-bulb-adjacent tissue; (C) orthogonal verification of intact-EV exposure in collected fluids/tissues (capture and particle counts); (D) prepare ex vivo tissue-derived microglia-like cells, apply standardized inflammatory challenge (LPS) and measure cytokine release with and without co-incubation with captured-fraction eluates; (E) compare cytokine responses across arms.
experiment.comparator: Four-arm comparison from the same conditioned-medium lot: (1) intact-EV-enriched preparation (capture-positive), (2) secretome-retaining concentrated conditioned medium, (3) intact-EV-enriched material treated with detergent + protease prior to administration (membrane-disrupted), (4) particle-count-matched but capture-depleted preparation (if achievable).
experiment.control: Positive control: characterized small EVs and dexamethasone in the ex vivo assay. Negative controls: vehicle-only and buffer fractions. Spike-in tracer and capture-compatibility buffer panels to exclude assay interference.
dependencies: Availability of sufficient conditioned-medium lots from the same source-cell bank and passage range
Validated immuno-capture reagents and particle-count instrumentation sensitivity for low-biomass lavage/CSF samples
Animal protocol approvals for short-interval tissue/fluid collection
Laboratory capability to run both orthogonal capture and ex vivo inflammatory assays with required throughput
experiment.failure_criterion: No reproducible linkage between in vivo orthogonal intact-EV verification and the ex vivo cytokine readout across replicates, or particle-count-matched capture-negative or membrane-disrupted arms produce equivalent ex vivo effects.
experiment.falsification_outcome: If failure criteria are met (and spike-in/capture compatibility controls validate assay performance), treat the material as functionally indistinguishable from secretome for the tested short-term ex vivo inflammatory readout and revise product-definition toward secretome-centric strategy; deprioritize EV-specific potency attribute.
experiment.hypothesis_tested: An intact-EV-associated, membrane-protected fraction (verified by capture + detergent/protease sensitivity and particle-peak co-localization) is necessary for a reproducible short-interval ex vivo CNS inflammatory modulation following intranasal administration; particle-count-matched but capture-negative or membrane-disrupted material will not produce the same ex vivo modulation.
experiment.primary_readout: Magnitude and reproducibility of ex vivo cytokine modulation (e.g., reduction in LPS-induced IL-6/TNF-α) from tissue-derived microglia-like cells correlated with in vivo orthogonal evidence of intact-EV exposure (presence of capture-positive signal and particle co-localization in lavage/CSF/tissue).
experiment.question: Can an orthogonal in vivo→ex vivo bridging experiment show that only capture-positive, membrane-protected material produces a reproducible short-interval ex vivo CNS inflammatory modulation after intranasal dosing, independent of bulk particle counts?
required_material: MSC-conditioned medium from a single characterized source-cell lot processed to produce: (A) enriched small-EV preparation (SEC/UC or program-defined bounded fraction) and (B) concentrated conditioned medium without EV enrichment (secretome-retaining)
Matched aliquots of capture-positive material treated with detergent + protease (membrane-disrupted) prior to administration
Particle-count instruments and reagents (NTA or TRPS)
Immuno-capture reagents for intact EV surface markers (anti-CD63/CD9/CD81 or TIM4/AnxA5)
Assays for orthogonal in vivo verification: capture from nasal lavage/CSF/olfactory mucosa homogenates and particle counts

Short-interval ex vivo CNS inflammatory assay platform (acutely harvested rodent olfactory-bulb/olfactory-mucosa-adjacent tissue processed to isolate microglia-like cells; LPS challenge; cytokine readouts such as IL-6/TNF-α ELISA or multiplex)
Exogenous intact-EV spike-in tracer (optional but recommended) to control for assay recovery
Protease (proteinase K), RNase reagents and detergent (Triton X-100 or equivalent) for membrane-disruption controls
Density-gradient materials (iodixanol) or SEC fractionation setup and fraction collectors
Total protein assay reagents and consumables
secondary_readouts: Co-localization metrics between particle-count peaks and capture-positive ELISA signal in administered material and in collected lavage/CSF fractions
Confirmation that captured material's activity is abolished by detergent + protease pre-treatment
Protein:particle ratios of administered materials and of captured fractions
Spike-in recovery percentage and membrane-protection behavior per fraction (if used)
Reproducibility across biological replicates (n ≥ 3 conditioned-medium preps and animal cohorts)
experiment.success_criterion: Qualitative success: In multiple independent conditioned-medium lots and animal cohorts (n ≥ 3), only the arm where administered material is orthogonally verified as capture-positive and shows particle-peak co-localization produces a reproducible reduction in ex vivo inflammatory cytokine readout; this reduction is abolished when captured material is membrane-disrupted prior to administration, and particle-count-matched capture-negative or secretome-retaining arms do not produce equivalent ex vivo modulation.

explicit_inferences: Rodent intranasal bioactivity warrants mechanistic translation studies but cannot alone justify intact-EV exposure claims in larger species.
An orthogonal in vivo→ex vivo bridge with membrane-protection controls is required to treat an orthogonal intact-EV signature as a potency-linked product attribute.
falsification_criteria: No reproducible linkage across independent lots/animal cohorts between in vivo orthogonal intact-EV verification and ex vivo cytokine modulation (i.e., capture-positive verification does not predict ex vivo effect).
Particle-count-matched but capture-negative or membrane-disrupted arms produce equivalent ex vivo effects, indicating activity is not intact-EV-associated.
human_decisions_required: Approve short-interval rodent in vivo protocol and sample collection plan.
Select exogenous intact-EV spike-in tracer (species or isotope-labeled) and harmonize capture-compatibility panels.
Decide whether to require particle-count-matched capture-depleted comparator (feasibility).
manufacturability_assessment: Demonstrating a mechanism-linked intact-EV attribute would enable a focused CMC pathway (orthogonal QC, mechanism-linked potency assay, comparability gates). If the bridge fails, program should reallocate resources to secretome-centric stability/formulation development and avoid EV-specific numeric specs.
manufacturing_rationale: If preserved, the mechanism-linked intact-EV attribute enables a potency-linked product-identity gate to guide fractionation, downstream process gates, and comparability testing; conversely, failure to link orthogonal intact-EV exposure to ex vivo effect argues for secretome-centric product definition and different CMC priorities.
measurement_strategy: Orthogonal characterization of administered materials (density/size fractionation + particle counts + immuno-capture + detergent/protease protection) pre-dose; intranasal dosing with short post-dose sampling; orthogonal verification of capture-positive particles in lavage/CSF/tissue; preparation of ex vivo microglia-like cells from harvested tissue for standardized inflammatory challenge and cytokine readout; compare arms including membrane-disrupted and capture-depleted controls; include exogenous intact-EV spike-in controls and capture-compatibility buffer panels.
novelty_statement: This proposal retains the program focus on an MSC-derived EV/secretome intranasal product but shifts the required discriminating experiment from purely analytic fractionation to an orthogonal in vivo→ex vivo bridge that uses membrane-protection controls and spike-in recovery to directly test whether an intact-EV-associated fraction is necessary for short-interval CNS immune modulation. This is a substantive change in the discriminating experiment (adds in vivo short-interval sampling and ex vivo functional readout) rather than a mere wording change.
principal_risks: Assay insensitivity or capture-reagent incompatibility producing false negatives in in vivo samples.
Failure to demonstrate linkage would necessitate pivoting away from EV-specific product definition.
Cross-species delivery barriers could prevent translation even if attribute is present in rodents.
proposed_potency_relationship: Presence of the intact-EV-associated, membrane-protected bioactivity predicts short-term ex vivo CNS inflammatory modulation and therefore serves as a candidate potency attribute for stage-1 bridging decisions; magnitude-response linking and numeric acceptance criteria require further validation.
proposed_product_change_or_attribute: Adopt a mechanism-linked potency gate defined as an intact-EV-associated, membrane-protected bioactivity that (A) co-localizes with capture-positive particle fractions in source material, (B) is abolished by detergent + protease/RNase treatment of captured material, and (C) is predictive of a short-interval ex vivo CNS inflammatory-response modulation after intranasal administration.
title: Required orthogonal in vivo→ex vivo bridge to test mechanism-linked potency for SGL-001
